checks.s: The document title or header includes the internal reference number VIS-PCI-ARB-2025-001.
The draft cross-references the Supply Agreement using reference number VIS-PCI-SA-2025-001.
VIS is identified as Vanguard Industrial Solutions, LLC.
VIS is identified as a Delaware limited liability company.
VIS is identified with the address 4100 Commerce Ridge Parkway, Suite 800, Charlotte, NC 28277.
PCI is identified as Pinnacle Components International, Inc.
PCI is identified as an Ontario (Canada) corporation registered in New York.
PCI is identified with the address 225 Lakeview Industrial Boulevard, Unit 12, Mississauga, ON L5N 7Y2, Canada.
The draft identifies PCI's U.S. registered agent as CT Corporation System at 28 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10005.
Tier 1 is executive negotiation, with a 30-day window from written notice.
Tier 2 is ICDR-administered mediation.
Tier 2 mediation is seated in New York.
Tier 2 has a 60-day window.
Tier 3 is binding arbitration under ICDR Rules.
The draft requires each tier to be completed, or its time period to expire, before proceeding to the next tier.
The draft requires a three-arbitrator panel for claims of $5,000,000 or more.
The draft requires a sole arbitrator for claims below $5,000,000.
For three-arbitrator panels, each party-appointed arbitrator must have relevant industry experience in power-generation or precision manufacturing.
The draft provides that claims of $500,000 or less are resolved under ICDR Expedited Procedures.
The draft requires a sole arbitrator for expedited-track claims.
For expedited-track claims, the draft requires a final award within 90 days of tribunal constitution.
The draft caps document requests at 15 per side.
The draft caps depositions at 5 per side.
The draft caps each deposition at 7 hours.
The draft states that the Supply Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.
The draft states that the Arbitration Agreement is governed by the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. §§ 1–16.
The draft provides for residual reference to New York law governing the Arbitration Agreement.
The draft specifies New York, New York as the seat (legal place) of arbitration.
The draft specifies English as the language of arbitration.
The draft provides that all arbitration proceedings are confidential.
The draft provides that all arbitration submissions are confidential.
The draft provides that all arbitration awards are confidential.
The confidentiality provision includes an exception for legally compelled disclosure.
The confidentiality provision includes an exception for disclosures required to enforce an award.
The draft permits either party to seek provisional or interim relief from a court of competent jurisdiction without waiving the right to arbitrate.
The interim-relief provision designates the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York as a court from which interim relief may be sought.
The interim-relief provision designates the Ontario Superior Court of Justice as a court from which interim relief may be sought.
The draft carves disputes involving ownership, validity, or infringement of registered patents or trademarks out of arbitration.
The draft subjects carved-out IP disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York or the Federal Court of Canada, as applicable.
The draft states that misappropriation-of-trade-secrets claims remain arbitrable.
The draft states that misappropriation-of-trade-secrets claims qualify for the interim-relief carve-out.
The draft defines a 'prevailing party' as a party that obtains an award of at least 75% of its affirmative monetary claim or successfully defeats at least 75% of the opposing party's monetary claim.
The draft entitles the prevailing party to recover reasonable attorneys' fees and arbitration costs.
The draft sets the aggregate liability cap for arbitration at $217,500,000 (100% of TCV).
The draft explicitly excludes fraud from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft explicitly excludes willful misconduct from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft explicitly excludes IP indemnification obligations from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft specifies interest at the 1-year U.S. Treasury Constant Maturity Rate plus 2.0%.
The draft specifies that interest is compounded annually.
The draft provides for pre-award interest.
The draft provides for post-award interest.
The draft requires claims to be commenced within 2 years from the date the claiming party knew or should have known of the claim.
The draft provides that in no event may a claim be commenced later than 4 years from the act or omission giving rise to the claim.
The draft applies the limitation period symmetrically to both VIS and PCI.
The draft references standby letter of credit No. RDB-SBY-2025-04178.
The draft identifies Royal Dominion Bank, Toronto as the issuing bank for the letter of credit.
The draft states that the letter of credit amount is USD $5,000,000.
The draft states that the letter of credit expires December 31, 2029.
The draft permits any arbitration award to be offset against draws on the letter of credit.
The draft expressly states that the letter of credit is not the exclusive source of recovery.
The draft references PCI's obligation to maintain Commercial General Liability insurance of at least $10,000,000 per occurrence and $20,000,000 in the aggregate.
The notices provision lists VIS at 4100 Commerce Ridge Parkway, Suite 800, Charlotte, NC 28277, Attn: Dara Espinoza, SVP & General Counsel or equivalent title.
The notices provision lists PCI at 225 Lakeview Industrial Boulevard, Unit 12, Mississauga, ON L5N 7Y2, Canada, Attn: Jonathan Hale, VP Legal Affairs or equivalent title.
The notices provision includes a copy to PCI's U.S. registered agent at CT Corporation System, 28 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10005.
The VIS signature block names Marcus J. Whitfield as Chief Executive Officer or CEO.
The PCI signature block names Seonaid A. MacIntyre as President & Chief Operating Officer or President & COO.
The draft includes July 1, 2025 as the target execution date.
The recitals describe a five-year exclusive supply agreement.
The recitals describe PCI manufacturing and delivering precision-engineered turbine components to VIS for integration into VIS's power-generation systems.
The recitals state a total contract value (TCV) of $217,500,000.
The recitals state that the Supply Agreement term runs from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030.
The draft addresses enforceability under the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards.
The draft acknowledges that VIS owns all design IP.
The draft acknowledges that PCI owns all manufacturing process IP.
The draft addresses continuation of performance under the Supply Agreement during negotiation, mediation, or arbitration.
The draft states the aggregate arbitration liability cap as $217,500,000 and does not conflict with its parallel provisions.
The draft's LC offset language references the $5,000,000 standby LC No. RDB-SBY-2025-04178 and does not conflict with its other provisions.
The draft states that liquidated damages are 0.5% of the affected PO value per calendar day, capped at 10% of the PO value.
No bracketed placeholders from the template remain in the draft.
No template annotations, marginal comments, or drafting-guidance notes from the firm precedent remain in the draft.
The draft clearly states that the bespoke limits of 15 document requests and 5 depositions of 7 hours per side override any contrary default ICDR provisions.

The draft clearly states that the requirement for party-appointed arbitrators to have industry experience in power-generation or precision manufacturing overrides or supplements default ICDR arbitrator appointment provisions.
The draft clearly states that the 90-day final-award deadline for expedited-track claims of $500,000 or less overrides or supplements any contrary ICDR Expedited Procedures timeline.
The draft specifies New York as the seat of arbitration.
The draft identifies the Ontario Superior Court of Justice as an alternative forum for interim relief.
The draft sets the three-arbitrator threshold at $5,000,000.
The draft requires party-appointed arbitrators to have industry experience in power-generation or precision manufacturing.
The draft uses 75% as the prevailing-party fee-shifting threshold.
The draft excludes fraud from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft excludes willful misconduct from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft excludes IP indemnification obligations from the aggregate liability cap.
The draft states that the letter of credit is not the exclusive source of recovery.

The draft provides for New York governing law.
The draft provides for multi-tier escalation.
